Today’s read

Teamlease Services Limited rose 5.6% on 134 times its usual volume. Its exchange filing that session was about guidance or investor update, “Schedule of meet”.

Sejal Glass Limited rose 10.3% on 123 times its usual volume. Its exchange filing that session was about guidance or investor update, “The Earnings Call for the Quarter and Half Year ended September 30, 2026.”.

Shoppers Stop Limited rose 2.9% on 454 times its usual volume, and it was in the news with “Indian mutual funds stop bulk subscriptions to gold ETFs ahead of festive season”.

Brent steady as US weighs easing sanctions on global shadow fleet
Washington is reviewing sanctions enforcement against maritime shadow tankers transporting Russian and Iranian oil. Unrestricted tanker availability sustains discounted crude imports for Indian refiners, protecting gross refining margins at Indian Oil and Bharat Petroleum. Lower landed oil costs also curb the national trade deficit, easing downward pressure on the rupee. Official US Treasury guidance on maritime enforcement will confirm the policy shift.

Indian mutual funds stop bulk subscriptions to gold ETFs ahead of festive season
Asset managers have restricted lump-sum cash subscriptions into gold exchange-traded funds ahead of Diwali, permitting only systematic investment plans. Physical sourcing bottlenecks and tracking errors against local spot prices drove the limitation. This development temporarily dampens bullion asset-under-management growth for listed managers such as Nippon Life India Asset Management and HDFC AMC, while preserving higher-margin retail systematic flows.

Market selloff, rising rates test AI data centre deal boom
Elevated global interest rates and debt market volatility are squeezing project financing for capital-intensive artificial intelligence data centres. Higher offshore borrowing costs lift capital expenditure hurdles for domestic infrastructure developers such as Bharti Airtel and Adani Enterprises. A slowdown in global enterprise infrastructure outlays also risks lengthening deal gestation periods for software exporters, including Tata Consultancy Services and Infosys.

US hyperscaler quarterly capital expenditure commentary remains the key metric to confirm any spending contraction.

Explainer: Why are credit default swaps unnerving AI investors?
Widening credit default swap spreads on debt issued by artificial intelligence infrastructure operators reflect rising default protection costs and investor skepticism over capital efficiency. Higher global credit risk premiums elevate offshore borrowing costs for Indian conglomerates funding domestic data centre builds through external commercial borrowings. Sustained credit spread expansion also threatens foreign institutional allocations to high-valuation domestic equities.

India's August balance of payments surplus swings to $45.4 billion
Capital inflows pushed India's August balance of payments surplus to $45.4 billion. A sustained surplus expands the Reserve Bank of India's foreign exchange reserves, shielding the rupee against currency volatility and adding liquidity to the banking system. Abundant systemic liquidity helps keep wholesale funding costs low for non-banking financial companies and private banks. Weekly reserve accretion figures will show whether the central bank absorbed these flows.

Pernod Ricard India sales grow 19% in Sept qtr; IPO plan awaits board approval
Pernod Ricard's Indian revenue grew 19 percent year-on-year in the September quarter, driven by premium whisky brands. This double-digit expansion confirms sustained consumer demand for prestige-and-above spirits, directly reading across to margin health and pricing power for listed peers United Spirits and Radico Khaitan. A formal board decision on the potential local listing will establish an updated valuation benchmark for Indian alcobev multiples.

Vikram Solar Subsidiary to Establish 7.5 GWh Battery Manufacturing Plant in Tamil Nadu - PSU India
A Vikram Solar subsidiary plans to build a 7.5 gigawatt-hour battery energy storage manufacturing facility in Tamil Nadu. Expanding domestic battery assembly lowers supply-chain risk and capital expenditure costs for renewable power producers, including Tata Power, JSW Energy, and Adani Green Energy, as grid-scale storage mandates take effect. Forthcoming cell supply contracts will determine whether the unit relies on imported chemistry or indigenous cells.

India's current account deficit narrows to $5.2 billion in August as capital account surplus hits $50.6 billion
India's current account deficit narrowed to $5.2 billion in August, while the capital account expanded to $50.6 billion on non-resident deposit inflows. A shrinking external deficit stabilizes the rupee and controls imported input costs for margin-sensitive sectors such as paints, specialty chemicals, and electronics manufacturing. September trade deficit merchandise numbers will confirm whether cooling non-oil import demand remains intact.

RBI clarifies interbank trades, ECBs coupons not part of FERR
The Reserve Bank of India clarified that foreign exchange risk reserve mandates exclude interbank market-making trades and external commercial borrowing coupon remittances. This exemption removes an overhang of punitive capital charges on bank treasury desks, protecting trading revenue for major lenders such as State Bank of India, ICICI Bank, and HDFC Bank. It also prevents additional intermediation costs for corporate borrowers servicing dollar-denominated debt.

Instead, it introduces a fresh peer comparison for listed gear and automation suppliers, directly testing relative valuation multiples for companies like Elecon Engineering and Shanthi Gears across industrial and construction equipment segments.

India revises fuel export duties, raises petrol tax and cuts diesel levy
The government raised export duties on petrol while reducing taxes on outbound diesel shipments under the windfall levy framework. The change directly shifts net refining realisations for private exporters, primarily Reliance Industries. Higher petrol taxes crimp overseas marketing margins on motor spirits, but the diesel levy cut offsets the hit by preserving refining spreads on middle distillates during high global price regimes.
